name: Amazon
summary: The largest river by volume, carrying about a fifth of all river water that reaches the ocean.
course: Rises in the Peruvian Andes and crosses Brazil to a mouth ~300 km wide; its freshwater plume extends hundreds of km into the Atlantic, and a reef system lies beneath it.
cycle: Annual flood pulse raises water by 10–15 m, flooding forests (várzea and igapó) for months.
life: Pink river dolphins, arapaima, piranhas, electric eels, Amazonian manatees, giant otters and over 3,000 fish species.
people: Supports Indigenous peoples and cities like Manaus and Belém.
threats: Deforestation, dams, mercury from gold mining, drought (record lows 2023–24).

name: Nile
summary: Often cited as the longest river, the lifeline of Egyptian civilisation.
course: White Nile from Lake Victoria and Blue Nile from Ethiopia join at Khartoum, ending in a large delta.
cycle: Historic summer flood from Ethiopian monsoon rains, now controlled by the Aswan High Dam (1970).
life: Nile crocodiles, Nile perch, hippos, migratory birds on the delta.
people: About 300 million people in 11 countries depend on it.
threats: Dams (including GERD), delta subsidence and saltwater intrusion.

name: Yangtze
summary: Asia's longest river and home to the Three Gorges Dam.
course: From the Tibetan Plateau to Shanghai.
life: Yangtze finless porpoise, Chinese sturgeon; the baiji is functionally extinct.
people: About 400 million people live in its basin.
threats: Dams, pollution, overfishing (10-year fishing ban from 2020).

name: Mississippi–Missouri
summary: North America's largest river system, draining ~40% of the contiguous USA.
course: Ends in the bird's-foot delta in Louisiana.
life: Paddlefish, alligator gar, catfish, migratory birds on the Mississippi Flyway.
people: A key shipping corridor for grain.
threats: Nutrient runoff causing the Gulf dead zone; delta land loss.

name: Yenisei
summary: The largest river flowing into the Arctic Ocean.
course: From Mongolia through Siberia.

name: Ob–Irtysh
summary: Siberian river with one of the longest estuaries (Gulf of Ob).
course: From the Altai mountains.

name: Lena
summary: Flows through permafrost to a vast Arctic delta.
course: Delta is a protected wildlife reserve.
cycle: Ice jams cause floods each spring.
threats: Warming and erosion of permafrost banks.

name: Congo
summary: The deepest river in the world (over 220 m) and second by discharge.
course: Its submarine canyon carries sediment ~1,000 km out to sea.
cycle: Crosses the equator twice, so it flows strongly year-round.
life: Over 700 fish species, many endemic to rapids; bonobos on its banks.

name: Mekong
summary: The world's largest inland fishery, flowing through six countries.
course: From Tibet to Vietnam's delta.
cycle: Flood pulse reverses Cambodia's Tonlé Sap river each year.
life: Mekong giant catfish, giant freshwater stingray, Irrawaddy dolphins.
people: About 60 million people depend on its fish.
threats: Over 100 dams, sand mining, sinking delta.

name: Ganges (Ganga)
summary: India's sacred river, forming with the Brahmaputra the world's largest delta.
course: From the Gangotri Glacier across the Indo-Gangetic Plain to the Sundarbans.
cycle: Monsoon floods supply most of its flow.
life: Ganges river dolphin, gharial, Ganges shark, hilsa, mahseer.
people: Over 500 million people in its basin.
threats: Pollution, dams and barrages (Farakka), groundwater loss.

name: Brahmaputra
summary: A braided giant flowing from Tibet through Assam and Bangladesh.
course: Called Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet; carves one of the deepest canyons on Earth.
cycle: Monsoon floods and huge sediment loads.
life: Ganges river dolphin, golden mahseer, Kaziranga floodplain wildlife.

name: Indus
summary: Cradle of the Harappan civilisation.
course: From Tibet through Ladakh and Pakistan.
threats: Delta starved of water and sediment.

name: Godavari
summary: India's second-longest river, the 'Dakshin Ganga'.
course: Across the Deccan Plateau to a delta in Andhra Pradesh.
life: Mangroves at Coringa, olive ridleys nearby.

name: Mahanadi
summary: Odisha's great river, feeding Chilika Lake area and the Bhitarkanika mangroves.
course: Flows from Chhattisgarh through Hirakud Dam to Odisha.
life: Saltwater crocodiles and olive ridleys near its delta.

name: Krishna
summary: A major Deccan river with mangroves at its mouth.
course: From the Western Ghats to Andhra Pradesh.

name: Narmada
summary: A west-flowing rift-valley river sacred in central India.
course: Through marble gorges at Bhedaghat.
threats: Dams reducing flow to the estuary.

name: Irrawaddy
summary: Myanmar's lifeline, home of the Irrawaddy dolphin.
course: North to south through Myanmar.
life: Irrawaddy dolphins that cooperate with fishers.

name: Zambezi
summary: Africa's fourth-longest river, plunging over Victoria Falls.
course: Through Zambia, Zimbabwe and Mozambique.
cycle: Seasonal floods; Kariba and Cahora Bassa dams.

name: Niger
summary: Flows in a boomerang through the Sahel to a vast oil-rich delta.
course: Inner Niger Delta wetlands in Mali.

name: Danube
summary: Europe's second-longest river, flowing through 10 countries.
course: From the Black Forest to a large delta in Romania.
life: Danube delta pelicans, beluga sturgeon migrations (blocked by dams).

name: Volga
summary: Europe's longest river.
course: Through Russia to the Caspian delta.

name: Rhine
summary: Western Europe's busiest waterway.
course: From the Alps through the Netherlands.

name: Thames
summary: London's river, once declared biologically dead (1957), now home to seals.
course: Estuary into the North Sea.

name: St. Lawrence
summary: Outlet of the Great Lakes, with one of the world's largest estuaries.
course: From Lake Ontario to the Atlantic.
life: Belugas, blue whales in the estuary.

name: Columbia
summary: Historically the greatest salmon river on Earth.
course: From British Columbia to Oregon.
life: Chinook and sockeye salmon, Pacific lamprey.

name: Yukon
summary: Home to one of the longest salmon migrations.
course: From Canada through Alaska.

name: Orinoco
summary: Venezuela's great river with a vast delta.
course: Connected to the Amazon by the Casiquiare channel.

name: Paraná
summary: South America's second-largest river.
course: Forms the Río de la Plata estuary.

name: Murray–Darling
summary: Australia's largest river system.
course: Ends at the Coorong lagoons.

name: Fly
summary: High-rainfall river of New Guinea.
course: Delta into the Gulf of Papua.

name: Pearl (Zhujiang)
summary: Forms the Pearl River Delta megacity region.
course: Estuary between Hong Kong and Macau.

name: Yellow (Huang He)
summary: The world's muddiest major river.
course: Through the Loess Plateau.
threats: Dry spells when it fails to reach the sea.

name: Amur
summary: Forms much of the Russia–China border.
course: Into the Tatar Strait.

name: Tigris–Euphrates
summary: The twin rivers of Mesopotamia.
course: Join as the Shatt al-Arab.

name: Kaveri (Cauvery)
summary: South India's sacred river, famous for mahseer.
course: From Coorg to Tamil Nadu's delta.

name: Hooghly
summary: Ganges distributary on which Kolkata stands.
course: Through West Bengal to the Bay.
